decision_table.name: Determine_UT_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Utah state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in UT (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
UT filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in UT if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in UT - Employees working in UT - Tangible personal property located in UT - Real property located in UT
Reference: UT Code § 59-7-102 (Definitions and nexus standards) Reference: Utah State Tax Commission Publication 25 (Nexus standards for corporations)

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
UT filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts in UT.
Note: As of July 1, 2025, UT removed the 200-transaction threshold per S.B. 47. Only the gross receipts threshold of $100,000 applies.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), UT requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus threshold, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: S.B. 47 (2025) - Economic nexus threshold changes Reference: Utah State Tax Commission Economic Nexus Guidance

No UT nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: UT Code § 59-7-102 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_UT_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate UT state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
UT state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
UT ADDITIONS to federal taxable income (Schedule B) include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to UT) - State income tax refunds included in federal taxable income - Expenses related to tax-exempt income - Other adjustments as specified in UT Code § 59-7-105
UT SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income (Schedule C) include: - Interest on UT state and municipal bonds (exempt for UT purposes) - State income taxes paid (not deductible for state purposes) - UT net operating loss deduction (subject to UT limitations) - Dividend income adjustments - Other adjustments as specified in UT Code § 59-7-106
Reference: Utah Form TC-20 Schedule B (Additions to Unadjusted Income) Reference: Utah Form TC-20 Schedule C (Subtractions from Unadjusted Income) Reference: UT Code § 59-7-105 (Additions to unadjusted income) Reference: UT Code § 59-7-106 (Subtractions from unadjusted income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have UT nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_UT_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate UT state corporate income tax. Applies UT 4.50% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
UT state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to UT: × [UT apportionment percentage] 3. UT additions: + [Federal interest, state tax refunds, etc.] 4. UT subtractions: - [UT municipal interest, state taxes paid, UT NOL, etc.] 5. UT taxable income: = [Result] 6. UT tax rate: × 4.50% 7. UT income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. UT credits: - [Renewable energy, research, economic development, etc.] 9. UT tax liability: = [Final tax]
UT uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
UT tax rate history: - 2025: 4.50% (reduced from 4.55% effective January 1, 2025) - 2024: 4.55% - 2023: 4.85% - 2022: 4.95% - Pre-2022: 5.00%
Utah has been progressively lowering its corporate income tax rate annually since 2022 as part of ongoing tax reform efforts.
UT provides various tax credits including: - Renewable energy systems tax credit - Research activities credit - Economic development tax credit - Historic preservation credit - Other credits as specified in UT Code Title 59, Chapter 7
Reference: Utah Form TC-20 (Corporation Franchise or Income Tax Return) Reference: UT Code § 59-7-104 (Tax rate of 4.50% effective 2025) Reference: UT Code § 59-7-311 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: Utah State Tax Commission Corporate Tax Publications

No UT nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in UT. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: UT Code § 59-7-102 (Nexus requirements)

No UT taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has UT nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
UT net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - UT allows NOL carryforward (generally follows federal rules) - NOL carryback provisions may apply in certain situations - Subject to UT-specific limitations and adjustments
Reference: Utah Form TC-20 (Corporation Franchise or Income Tax Return) Reference: UT Code § 59-7-110 (Net operating loss deduction)
